newsitem.title: CANADA: IPL restarts more crude oil pipelines.
newsitem.headline: IPL restarts more crude oil pipelines.

text.p: IPL Energy Inc unit Interprovincial Pipe Line said on Tuesday that it restarted more pipelines on its system after its major shutdown.

Line 1, which moves natural gas liquids and petroleum products to Superior, Wisconsin from Edmonton, Alberta, was restarted Tuesday afternoon and was moving partial volumes after power was restored to one pumping station at Viking in Minnesota, IPL spokesman Alan Roth said.
"The expections from power companies in the States is that the rest of the Line 1 units will be up later today," Roth said.
He said Line 1 was expected to be back up to full capacity on Wednesday.
Line 2A, which carries crude oil to Cromer, Manitoba from Edmonton, was restarted on Tuesday and was flowing at reduced rates, Roth said.
Line 2B, the second leg of the line that extends to Superior was brought bak into partial service earlier in the day.
Line 6A on the affiliated Lakehead system, which moves Canadian oil to Chicago from Superior was also restarted, he said.
Line 6B, the extension to Sarnia, Ontario from Chicago, was expected to resume pumping once more crude oil was available to ship.

Lakehead's Line 5, which runs to Sarnia from Wisconsin via north of Lake Michigan, was still shut down on Tuesday because of low inventories left in IPL's tanks at Superior. The stocks were drained after the outage, which was caused by a power failure which knocked out pumping stations in Minnesota.
The line was scheduled to restart some time Wednesday, Roth said.
Line 13 to Superior from Hardisty Alberta, downstream from Edmonton, also remained down on Tuesday.
"Line 13 was scheduled to be shut down anyway...there wasn't a lot of product sheduled for that anyway," he said.
The other major artery, Line 3 to Superior from Edmonton, was restarted at partial rates earlier on Tuesday.
